For inverted dropout with drop probability p, x̃=m⊙x/(1−p), where m has Bernoulli(1−p) entries. Conditional on x, E[x̃−x]=0 and E‖x̃−x‖²=p/(1−p)‖x‖²; this follows directly from the scaling documented by [PyTorch](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.Dropout.html). Consequently, equal dropout probabilities on item and positional embeddings generally inject unequal perturbation energy. A derived energy-matched control chooses p_c=E/(S_c+E), where S_c is the component’s measured mean squared norm at the injection point, including any embedding scaling and excluding padding. Estimate S_c on training data and report realized energy as norms evolve. Item-only dropout gains establish an intervention effect under that configuration; they do not alone establish component-specific importance. Even energy matching leaves differences in noise covariance, downstream sensitivity, and interactions with normalization.

For paired training comparisons, use separate random streams for initialization, batch ordering, negative sampling, existing dropout, and experimental dropout; synchronize corresponding streams across variants. An added dropout call can otherwise advance a shared generator and change subsequent random inputs despite identical initial seeds. [Common-random-number research](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3725537/) emphasizes that separate streams also require synchronization by event. Practical implication: give experimental masks a dedicated generator and align shared draws by training step or example. Independent streams are needed between randomness sources; matched streams are useful across compared variants. Repeat matched seed pairs and report paired validation differences; one paired run cannot establish robustness.
